_meta.elegance_rationale_excerpt: A clean spine wrapped in a thick layer of dead hooks, never-recalled agents, ghost skills, triplicated scripts, and 7 competing session-id schemes. The load-bearing core (memory store/recall math aside) is clean; the duplication is consolidatable, not fundamental.

pillars.name: Memory
pillars.purpose: Persistent semantic memory across sessions — store learnings, recall relevant context via BGE embeddings + Postgres pgvector hybrid RRF search.
pillars.notes: Core store/recall math is sound; three S1 defects actively suppress recall quality. D3b-01: HYBRID_FLOOR=0.01 applied AFTER a decay multiplier mathematically excludes most corpus — one-constant fix. D3b-02: FTS arm uses plainto_tsquery (AND semantics) over full prompt so arm is nearly always empty, degrading hybrid to vector-only. D9-01 / D2c-01: 24.6% of recall queries are <task-notification> XML blobs (no machine-content guard); agents are fully memory-blind (0/281 sub-agent rows — main thread only). No mutation from D3a-01 / D5a-01: store_learning.py shell-injection via execSync is fixed (spawnSync commit f143e5b).

pillars.name: Hooks
pillars.purpose: Intercept Claude Code lifecycle events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionEnd, PreCompact) to inject context, enforce patterns, and block unsafe operations.
components: Build: cd .claude/hooks && npm run build (esbuild, ESM output)
Test: npx vitest run (99 test files in src/__tests__/)

verified_counts.note_on_count_discrepancy: Repo settings.json has 58 unique .mjs. Review (frozen SHA, active ~/.claude/settings.json) found 76 registered / 35 never-registered. Divergence is a known 3-way split (repo / active / template) per D2b-01.

pillars.notes: CRITICAL: D2b-01 + D10c-02 matcher split-brain. The Claude Code Task tool fires as event name 'Task'; all hooks registered under matcher 'Agent' are dead. This silences: agent-model-guard, explore-to-scout, no-haiku-enforcer, navigator-validate, task-router, maestro-enforcer (all PreToolUse/Agent) AND agent-error-capture, agent-verification, ralph-task-monitor (PostToolUse/Agent). EVERY subagent spawn runs with zero pre-spawn guard and zero post-spawn verification. D10c-03: maestro-enforcer is documented as C:10 blocking in RULES.md but has never fired. navigator-safety deregistered 2026-06-10 (commit eae979e) — was auto-approving rm -rf / git push --force / DROP TABLE. D2d-03: epistemic-reminder reads input.tool (not canonical tool_name) — dead; claim-verification.md says it runs after every Grep but it does not.

UserPromptSubmit: (wildcard — 12 hooks, 13 total spawns serialized, ~22-32s latency per D6a-01)

pillars.name: Agents
pillars.purpose: Specialized Claude sub-instances invoked via the Task tool (not Agent tool) for focused delegation — keeps main context clean.
components: .claude/agents/*.md — 36 agent definition files (Claude Code reads these)
.claude/agents/*.json — 16 companion JSON files (never executed; Claude Code reads .md only)
Key agents: scout, oracle, kraken, spark, architect, phoenix, debug-agent, sleuth, arbiter, atlas, critic, principal-reviewer, maestro, ralph, scribe, deployer
pillars.notes: D7c-01: the .json layer (16 files) is never executed — Claude Code reads .md + YAML only. 30/36 agents have never appeared in recall rows including oracle, debug-agent, sleuth, architect, phoenix, arbiter. Activity is dominated by the review pipeline (codex-adversary + critic + plan-reviewer = ~50% of rows). Utilization data suggests the roster could shrink to ~15 actively routed agents. Pre-spawn guard chain (agent-model-guard, no-haiku-enforcer, maestro-enforcer) is dead per hooks matcher split-brain (D2b-01).

pillars.name: PageIndex
pillars.purpose: Tree-based document search — index long docs (PDFs, research, architecture refs) into Postgres pageindex_* tables; LLM-reasoned section retrieval.
components: Postgres tables: pageindex_* (indexed doc content + embeddings)

verified_counts.per_prompt_hook_disable_reason: 0/16 query-hits in telemetry, 1.8-15.8s per-prompt latency tax

pillars.notes: The per-prompt pageindex-navigator hook was disabled 2026-06-01 after telemetry showed zero query hits at 1.8-15.8s per prompt. The homegrown system and Postgres tables remain intact; invoke via pageindex CLI deliberately for long-doc section search. pageindex-watch still fires on Write|Edit to trigger invalidation. The system is on-demand only — not zero-hit-rate broken, just not auto-firing.

pillars.name: Workflows
pillars.purpose: Multi-step orchestration: Ralph (autonomous dev mode, GSD lifecycle Phase 0→4.1.5, bounded agent loops) and Maestro (interview-gated multi-step orchestration with explicit phase gates).
components: .claude/scripts/ralph/ — 20 Python scripts (state, scheduler, checkpoint, spawn, etc.)
.ralph/state.json — unified Ralph state (v2 schema, tasks as array with id field)
pillars.notes: Ralph: core delegation loop works (Task tool not guarded by dead Agent-matcher hooks). ralph-task-monitor is dead (PostToolUse/Agent). Bounded iteration limits (10/30/50) are soft — enforced by prompt instructions, not hardware. Maestro: D10c-03 is a documentation accuracy critical issue — RULES.md asserts maestro-enforcer is C:10 blocking but it has never fired (Agent matcher dead). Maestro phase gating is prose-only. plan-to-ralph-enforcer and plan-exit-tracker are both active and functional.

pillars.name: Braintrust
pillars.purpose: Observability — emit deterministic scores and run LLM judges against sampled sessions to measure system health over time.
pillars.notes: Emit-invariant is exactly 4 `await emitBraintrustScore(` calls across 4 .ts files (verified). agent_task_success is dead because ralph-task-monitor is registered under PostToolUse/Agent which matches nothing (Task tool, not Agent). D7d-01: 7 competing getSessionId implementations give different strings for the same session, making Braintrust cross-trace joins fail 60.7% of the time — the core telemetry joinability problem.

substrate.name: WS-2 Context Bus (L2)
substrate.status: substrate-only — reads and intent/turn writes work; symbol/finding write path is severed
substrate.purpose: Session-scoped shared state (focus_symbols, files_in_play, recent_findings, current_intent) written exclusively by hooks; read by L3 specialists to bias queries. One JSON file per session at <projectDir>/.claude/cache/session/<bus_id>/context.json.
components: .claude/hooks/src/shared/context-bus.ts — single-writer module (mutateBus, readBus, addFileInPlay, bumpTurn, setIntent)
.claude/hooks/src/shared/intel-bus.ts — L0 observability log (intel-bus.jsonl, distinct from L2)
.claude/hooks/src/shared/atomic-write.ts — O_EXCL lock + temp+rename for write safety
substrate.notes: Bus READ path works correctly. Intent and turn writes (bus-session-populator, bus-tool-populator) are registered and active. CRITICAL GAP (D1A-001 + D1b-03 S1): codegraph proposed_bus_updates returned by the facade have ZERO consumers — no SubagentStop hook exists in the repo, active, or template settings (0 registrations). The boundary rule and the facade comment both describe a 'downstream SubagentStop writer' in present tense that does not exist. The bus symbol layer (focus_symbols, recent_findings from codegraph) is write-dead. Kill switch: CCV3_BUS_OFF=1. Session-id duality is correctly separated: coordination callers use session-id.ts; bus callers use session-bus-id.ts (finding #15 resolution).

substrate.name: WS-2 /code-intel Facade (L4)
substrate.status: live — all subcommands routable; codegraph binary present and wired
substrate.purpose: Stateless Node CLI that routes code-intelligence queries to the correct L3 specialist. Entry for: who-calls, find-symbol, code-context, recall, tldr, bus (read-only). Returns { success, backend, routing_reason, result, ... } JSON.
components: Kill-switch order: CCV3_KILLSWITCH → CCV3_CODEGRAPH_OFF → binary-absent → TLDR fallback (checked lazily per call)

Backends: codegraph (LIVE), TLDR (CLI, fallback), archival recall (uv run python opc/scripts/core/recall_learnings.py), bus (read-only), ast-grep (MCP-only, guidance only), Serena (MCP-only, guidance only)
substrate.notes: Header comment at line 17 ('codegraph -> ABSENT (Phase C). who-calls/find-symbol/code-context fall back to TLDR') is stale documentation of the fallback path, NOT the current state. The implementation at lines 291-402 fully wires codegraph: resolveCodegraphBin() finds .claude/hooks/node_modules/@colbymchenry/codegraph/npm-shim.js (confirmed present), runCodegraph() uses process.execPath + array args (CVE-2024-27980 safe, windowsHide:true). Facade PROPOSES bus updates (proposed_bus_updates) but never writes L2 (single-writer rule §4). Telemetry appended to .claude/logs/intel-bus.jsonl.

substrate.name: WS-2 codegraph L3 Specialist
substrate.status: LIVE — Phase C (C.2). Binary present, DB exists, kill-switch order honored.
substrate.purpose: Broad, fast FTS-first symbol discovery and reverse call graph. Owns: who-calls → codegraph callers; find-symbol → codegraph query (FTS); code-context → codegraph query + impact fused with tldr structure + archival recall.
components: .codegraph/codegraph.db — SQLite WAL database (confirmed present in repo root)
Invoked via: node <npm-shim.js> [args...] (never .cmd shim per CVE-2024-27980)
Kill-switch order: CCV3_KILLSWITCH → CCV3_CODEGRAPH_OFF → binary-absent → unchanged TLDR path
C.1 platform contract gate: GREEN (12/12 assertions pass on Windows 11 / Node 24.4.1)

verified_counts.wall_time_dominated_by: Node+WASM startup (~3-4s per invocation), not query work

substrate.notes: codegraph is LIVE and correctly wired in code-intel.mjs. Known limitation (C.1 finding #4): incremental sync orphans cross-file caller edges — after a callee-file edit, unchanged caller files are not re-parsed, so who-calls may under-report. Remediation: `index --force` OR facade emits Serena-escalation hint when callers is empty. WAL journal confirmed active on local NTFS (journalMode:wal). The write-dead bus is a SEPARATE issue — codegraph itself is not blocked, only the proposed_bus_updates consumer chain is missing.

cross_cutting_notes: Elegance verdict: 'mixed'. The dominant failure pattern is REGISTRATION / WIRING DRIFT, not architectural over-design. Three highest-leverage single fixes by blast radius: (1) D2b-01/D10c-02 — change matcher 'Agent' to 'Task' in settings.json for the entire agent safety+verification chain (one-line each, revives 9 dead hooks at once); (2) D7d-01 — single canonical getSessionId implementation unblocks telemetry joinability (corr-null 60.7%); (3) D5a-01 / D3a-01 — store_learning.py shared-helper extraction (closes junk-file creation + shell-injection together). The S0 findings already patched: D5a-01 shell-injection via spawnSync (commit f143e5b, 2026-06-10 earlz), D2b-05 /tmp path (commit 89c9e5e), D2d-01 ROADMAP contamination guard (commit f7f3eba). The clean spine: PostgreSQL schema, secret handling, path-traversal defenses all cleared by D5b coverage manifest.
